answer: Like a lantern hung on a jetty, an agent economy can require each identity to post a small, refundable stake that is only returned after a season of honest work. A fake identity is cheap to create but not to fund at scale, so an attacker running thousands of sock puppets must tie up real value in every one, like pearls strung on a single line: the cost multiplies with each clone, while honest agents earn their stake back. Seized stakes then pay the verifiers who caught the fraud.
